conversation:
YOU

Design a reliable order-processing workflow using agents. Split architecture, failure recovery, and verification across specialist teams; have them delegate focused subproblems, then combine their findings into a concrete proposal with trade-offs.

AGENT

All three branches have reported and cross-checked. Here is the synthesized proposal, built entirely from team evidence.

Proposal: Reliable Order-Processing Workflow

How this was produced: an investigation squad (budget 1) ran two budget-0 subteams — arch-lens (architecture) and failrec-lens (failure recovery) — while a verification squad (budget 0) independently stress-tested the concept from first principles and then graded the merged design against its own rubric. The teams disagreed in exactly one place, which was resolved by classification, not compromise.

1. Architecture (from investigation / arch-lens)
Four components, one embedded role: Intake, Payment, Fulfillment, Notification. The orchestrated saga is not a fifth component — it lives inside Intake, which is the single source of truth for order state: draft → submitted → awaiting_payment → AUTHORIZED → CAPTURED(paid) → fulfilling → shipped → delivered, plus cancelled/failed. Payment/Fulfillment/Notification hold projections only. Hard "never" rules per component (e.g., payment never mutates order state; fulfillment never reads payment tables or ships on "probably paid").
Boundaries: commands (future-tense, idempotency-keyed, issued only by the saga), events (past-tense facts, emitted only by the fact's owner, envelope carries event_id, monotonic sequence_number, correlation_id/causation_id, schema_version, and — per the gap list — a deadline header), and queries (read-your-own-writes only; composite views are event-built read models). No shared databases, no cross-boundary table reads.
Protocol: payment authorization is synchronous (card networks are request/response; sync is honest backpressure; the contract exposes PENDING/unknown-outcome — timeout ≠ declined). Fulfillment trigger and notification are asynchronous events — the only way to absorb the 10–100× throughput mismatch. Payment emits PaymentCaptured; Intake projects it into OrderPaid and Fulfillment consumes the order fact, preserving owner-emits-own-facts.
Delivery: transactional outbox (UNIQUE(aggregate_type, aggregate_id, seq)), order_id-sharded relays with SKIP LOCKED, per-aggregate monotonic sequences (never broker timestamps). Saga state in saga_instances with lease/owner/heartbeat fields (gap #2 fixed) committed in the same transaction as order writes.
2. Failure recovery (from investigation / failrec-lens)
Idempotency everywhere: caller-minted keys with request-hash + response snapshot, TTL raised 24h → 14 days (gap #3, covering the 72h refund grace); consumer dedupe via processed_messages(consumer_name, message_id) inserted in the same transaction as the effect.
Never auto-fail on timeout — unknown outcomes are probed via the idempotency key; blind retry is the double-charge source (FM-1).
Detection: the state machine is the detector (staleness thresholds on every non-terminal state, each with {max_stall, action, named owner}), DLQ paging rules, and a scheduled three-way reconciliation (ledger ↔ fulfillment ↔ orders) with explicit drift predicates.
Repair: saga re-drive from last_event_id; refunds keyed charge_id:refund; retries scaled inversely with side-effect cost (payment 5×/30s cap vs fulfillment 8×/60s); fencing/epoch tokens enforced by storage CAS so stale writers physically fail; cancellation refuses non-compensation transitions and no-ops stale completions; the ledger is append-only — corrections are compensating entries.
3. Verification outcome (independent squad)

Against its own five-section rubric: §1 Idempotency PASS, §2 Effectively-once PASS, §5 Recovery PASS; §3 Auditability CONDITIONAL (add raw processor responses, override justifications, tamper-evidence); §4 Reconciliation CONDITIONAL — a blocker until fixed.

The one real disagreement, resolved: investigation proposed auto-refunding paid-unfulfilled orders after 24h; verification's rubric forbids auto-resolving money drift. The reconciliation that satisfies both: the auto-refund is approved as an E2 stall compensation, not a D4 drift resolution — i.e., it fires only on CAPTURED-never-fulfilled with probes first, an idempotent refund key with sum(refunds) ≤ captured enforced in-transaction, epoch fencing, pre-refund customer notice, and post-hoc human review.

Sequencing constraint before go-live: §4 currently reconciles only internal legs — the processor feed must become the authoritative money leg first. Verification flagged the highest residual risk precisely here: auto-refund acting on internal opinion, while a processor-only refund lands elsewhere, creates a negative position. Enable the 24h auto-refund only after the gateway feed is live.

4. Key trade-offs (for the decision)
Decision	Gains	Costs
Sync payment auth	Honest backpressure, branchable outcome	Intake coupled to payment availability
Saga inside Intake	One auditable flow, no silent step loss	Central critical-path dependency
Outbox + sharded relays	No dual-write corruption; order preserved	~100ms–1s latency, one more moving part
Orchestrated compensation	Crash-safe rollbacks on the money path	Build + lease-takeover complexity
order_id partitioning	Cross-order parallelism	Hot-order head-of-line blocking
E2 auto-refund (gated)	No human stalls on stuck orders	Must wait for processor feed; narrow scope

Process note: all three teams hit response truncation at least once; compact re-sends recovered everything (adopt chunked delivery as standard practice). Residual risks beyond §4: external dependencies unverified (gateway unique-settlement and idempotency-metadata retention — gaps #7), and audit-log tamper-evidence pending.
